text:
Samir: Quick thread — I'm running a pairwise smokebench to compare two model variants with strict apples-to-apples decoding and tokenizer alignment. Goal: surface any latency/regression caused by kernel selection or KV reuse differences and validate identical outputs for our short prompt set.
Maya: Which models and which harness? short prompts or replay?
Samir: models: rw-base-8b (float16) vs rw-base-8b-q4 (quant). Harness: pairwise replay (we'll feed exact tokenized prefixes). Using the small prompt set (200 short prompts) to keep runs fast.
Jon: Make sure tokenizer is deterministic — use the same tokenizer binary and vocab. We had a sneaky mismatch last quarter (different pretokenize flags).
Li: Also pin decode params: temperature=0.0, top_k=1, stop=["\n"]. No sampling. That guarantees deterministic decode given same logits.
Samir: Yep. Repro command I'm using:
```bash
./harness/pairwise_run.sh \
  --model-a rw-base-8b \
  --model-b rw-base-8b-q4 \
  --prompts data/short_prompts.jsonl \
  --decode "temp=0.0,top_k=1,stop=[\\"\\n\\"]" \
  --kv-reuse true \
  --batch-size 8 \
  --concurrency 32 \
  --profile perf/trace.json
```
Maya: what platform? kernel selection can change between CUDA/ROCm/MLIR.
Samir: linux-dedicated-gpu pool (A100), docker image rwinf/serving:2026-02. Kernel selector is enabled (auto).
Sophia: Can you also run with kernel_selector=force_naive to see where heuristics pick a different kernel? small tweak but helps root cause.
Samir: Good idea. I'll run both auto and force_naive and diff.
perf-bot: Initial run (auto) finished: mean p95 latency per request: 128ms (rw-base-8b), 112ms (q4). Token throughput: 4600 tps vs 4850 tps. KV miss rate: 0.0 (replay). Save at perf/runs/1791234567/auto.json :point_down:
perf-bot: {"artifact":"perf/runs/1791234567/auto.json","summary":"p50:98ms,p95:128ms,mean:115ms,throughput:4730tps"}
Jon: Nice. But the q4 being faster — check kernel selection logs for conv/fused attention choice. Might be doing different GEMM path.
Samir: Kernel logs show: rw-base-8b chose kernel=v1_gemm_fused_attn, rw-base-8b-q4 chose kernel=v1_quant_gemm_fast.
Li: Any output deltas? With temp=0 and top_k=1 we expect identical outputs if tokenization is identical.
Samir: I ran a diff on generated tokens: 199/200 exact match. One mismatch: prompt #127 diverged at token 3. Investigating.
Maya: That's concerning. Could be KV cache flushing or different kv layout in q4 path. Did you enable kv_cache_compression?
Samir: kv_cache_compression=false for both. I inspected the logs: on mismatch run, q4 path emitted a short warning: "kv-index-roundtrip-truncation" — looks like an integer cast in the quant path.
Sophia: If it's a quant path rounding issue, add an ips-level assert: run identical random seeds and also run a synthetic replay that forces cache hits to validate.
Samir: Ran with synthetic prefix replay (all cache hits). Both models matched 200/200. So divergence only occurs in mixed cache warmup where q4 path uses a different KV packing algorithm.
Jon: Open an issue and tag eng-runtime/infra. This could be a correctness edge-case in the quant kernel's KV serializer.
Samir: Filed: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-8912 — attached perf logs and the one-divergent sample.
perf-bot: Comparison (force_naive run) finished: p95 increased by ~20ms for both, q4 now matches outputs 200/200. Saved at perf/runs/1791234567/force_naive.json
Maya: So heuristics pick faster kernels but introduce a subtle kv layout bug. Prioritize correctness > perf. For next steps: 1) add unit test covering kv-index-roundtrip with q4 packing, 2) add a parity harness that runs short deterministic prompt sets in CI on all kernel_selector modes, 3) add a regression alert when token-match fraction < 100% on deterministic decode.
Li: I'll take (1) and (2). Jon can you help with (3) in the console alerting rules?
Jon: Yep, I'll add a per-commit check and a dashboard panel that surfaces token-match-rate by model+kernel.
Samir: Thanks. I'll schedule a follow-up after Li's unit tests land. :thumbsup:
Maya: Thanks for running the clean pairwise bench. This pattern should be our go-to for apples-to-apples compare going forward — strict tokenization, deterministic decode, kv-hit synthetic control, and kernel-selector toggles.
Sophia: Also worth adding a tiny replay harness mode that injects kernel_selector=force_naive automatically whenever token-match < 100% to make triage faster.
Samir: Noted. Closing thread when the fix is merged.
